## What students learn

Students review one parallel circuit, then identify a series circuit as one continuous path, calculate total resistance and current, calculate each voltage drop, check the result with Kirchhoff's voltage law, and apply resistor power ratings.

## Why it matters

Series analysis lets students predict a circuit before they build it, check measurements, and recognize when a result cannot be correct.

## Notes and equations

[Open the Series Circuits notes](../../circuits/series-circuits.qmd)

The website notes use LaTeX for the general series rules:

$$
I_k = I_T
$$

$$
R_T = \sum_{k=1}^{n} R_k
$$

$$
V_T = \sum_{k=1}^{n} V_k
$$

## Learning route

1. Show a complete low-voltage series system before introducing equations.
2. Watch the short conceptual introduction and predict what one open component will do.
3. Move from the physical build to the schematic.
4. Compare one series path with parallel branches.
5. Learn the current, resistance, voltage, and power rules.
6. Complete one guided GUESS example with separate Given and Unknown sections.
7. Enter each calculator step on a separate line.
8. Complete one parallel-review question and five progressively harder series questions, submitting one photo for each.
9. Verify the rules with the adapted Grob Experiment 4-1 circuit.

## Experiment 4-1 adaptation

Use a current-limited 10.0 V direct-current supply, a breadboard, a fused digital multimeter, test leads, jumper wires, and 1.0 kΩ, 2.2 kΩ, and 3.3 kΩ resistors. No software is required; Tinkercad can be used as an optional pre-lab.

Students calculate and measure total resistance, current at four points, each voltage drop, the voltage-law check, and percent difference. They submit one clear circuit photo.

Power must be off for resistance measurements. The ammeter must be connected in series. Do not create a deliberate hard short.

[Open Experiment 4-1: Series Circuits](https://drive.google.com/file/d/10eVEuQ5qLZKLGSWI0tIA8n_mbo_TYQ2B/view){target="_blank"}<br>
[Open Experiment 4-2: Series Circuits - Resistance](https://drive.google.com/file/d/10YkhmOECyUzPF_oUh4Erqb1SjhIlKekT/view){target="_blank"}

Experiment 4-2 is a useful resistance-focused extension after the core investigation.
